title: EDGAR ↔ GLEIF — company-to-LEI crosswalk
description: A resolved crosswalk linking SEC EDGAR registrants (CIK / ticker / fund series) to their GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) — one row per asserted identity, each carrying its provenance tier, method and confidence. Authoritative edges come from official SEC/GLEIF registration (no guessing); the operating-company tail is linked by probabilistic name resolution (Fellegi-Sunter / Splink): exact normalized-name matches are confirmed (~95% precision), while name-only fuzzy matches are surfaced as candidates rather than auto-confirmed. A point-in-time snapshot, with an as-of date on every row.

key_type.description: Scheme of the SEC identifier held in `key`, and the discriminator that says how to read that column. This snapshot carries two: cik (an EDGAR Central Index Key, rendered as decimal digits) and series (an SEC fund identifier, a letter prefix followed by digits). A third scheme, class (fund share class), is producible by the pipeline but is absent from this snapshot.

key.description: The SEC-side identifier this edge is keyed on, read according to `key_type`: for cik rows an EDGAR Central Index Key in decimal digits with no leading zeros; for series rows an SEC fund identifier — an uppercase letter prefix followed by digits (S…, CEF…). Text, not a number: the two schemes share one column, so the pattern above is their union and no arithmetic type describes it. To join it to `edgar.cik`, render that integer column as text — see `x-joins`.

lei.description: GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442): a four-character alphanumeric LOU prefix, fourteen alphanumeric entity characters, then two check digits — ISO 7064 MOD 97-10 over the eighteen that precede them. The `pattern` below states the shape and nothing more: no regular expression evaluates a checksum, and `00000000000000000000` satisfies this one. The arithmetic is checked where the edge is built: `models/load.sql` declares it and `models/package.sql` gates the terminal table on it. A value GLEIF publishes is admitted whether or not its check digits satisfy the standard, because the register defines which identifiers exist.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction the entity is constituted under, as GLEIF records it: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, or an ISO 3166-2 subdivision code (country, hyphen, subdivision) where GLEIF holds one — US-DE, AE-SH. The type on this field is declared by Meridian, not inferred: finetype returns `geography.location.state_code` on 260 of 300 independent 100-value samples of this column, and geography.location.country_code on 34 and unknown on 6, so an inferred label here is a draw. `x-finetype-confidence` on this field is that agreement rate over 300 samples, NOT a model score for a single run.

category.description: GLEIF's authoritative entity category (e.g. GENERAL, FUND, BRANCH); GENERAL when unknown.

method.description: How the edge was established. Authoritative: sec-registration (GLEIF RA000665) or sec-ncen (SEC Form N-CEN). Probabilistic: exact_name (identical normalized company name) or jaro_winkler (fuzzy name).

tier.description: Provenance tier, in precedence order: authoritative (deterministic SEC/GLEIF registration — no guessing), confirmed (exact normalized-name Splink match, ~95% precision), candidate (name-only fuzzy match, surfaced NOT asserted), ambiguous (one exact name matched more than one entity). A deterministic edge always wins over a name match for the same key. The type on this field is declared by Meridian, not inferred: finetype returns `representation.text.word` on 193 of 300 independent 100-value samples of this column, and datetime.component.month_name on 107, so an inferred label here is a draw. `x-finetype-confidence` on this field is that agreement rate over 300 samples, NOT a model score for a single run.

confidence.description: Edge confidence in [0, 1]: 1.0 for authoritative edges; the Fellegi-Sunter posterior match probability under the frozen resolution model for probabilistic edges.

corpus.description: Lowercased, accent-stripped concatenation of the display name, legal name, ticker and LEI — a derived free-text search field, not a source attribute. The type on this field is declared by Meridian, not inferred: finetype returns `representation.text.plain_text` on 186 of 300 independent 100-value samples of this column, and unknown on 75, alphanumeric_id on 37 and semicolon_separated on 2, so an inferred label here is a draw. `x-finetype-confidence` on this field is that agreement rate over 300 samples, NOT a model score for a single run.

reg_status.description: The type on this field is declared by Meridian, not inferred: finetype returns `representation.text.word` on 262 of 300 independent 100-value samples of this column, and geography.location.state_code on 38, so an inferred label here is a draw. `x-finetype-confidence` on this field is that agreement rate over 300 samples, NOT a model score for a single run.

company_name.description: The type on this field is declared by Meridian, not inferred: finetype returns `representation.text.entity_name` on 246 of 300 independent 100-value samples of this column, and unknown on 36, plain_text on 14 and full_address on 2, so an inferred label here is a draw. `x-finetype-confidence` on this field is that agreement rate over 300 samples, NOT a model score for a single run.

as_of.description: The date this linkage was asserted — the vintage of the sources the edge was resolved from, stamped on every row at build time. Constant within any one published build, and that is the point: an edge carries its own vintage, so a row copied out of this table into a warehouse still says when it was true, and two builds unioned together stay tellable apart. The package's top-level `created` records when the descriptor was written, which is a different fact and does not travel with the rows. A link is a claim about two identifiers at a moment: EDGAR registrants change name and CIK, LEIs lapse and transfer, and an edge resolved in July is not evidence about December. Read it as the as-at date for the claim, not as a modification timestamp.

x-joins.$comment: How to join this crosswalk to the packages it references, and how far each join reaches. These are NOT `schema.foreignKeys`: a Data Package foreign key asserts that every value on the left exists on the right, and neither of these joins satisfies that against the published bytes — see each `cardinality` and (in the built descriptor) `coverage`. Declaring them as foreign keys would advertise a guarantee the data does not keep, so the guarantee is dropped and the reachable part is stated instead. `coverage` does NOT live in this file: a hand-typed row count decays as soon as an upstream source grows, which is exactly what happened here (four weeks stale on 2026-08-13). `crosswalk_join.py --write` measures it from the build and writes it into the generated `datapackage.json` instead.

joins.cardinality: partial — most left rows have no match, and the referenced side also holds keys this crosswalk does not carry. Neither side contains the other.
joins.description: SEC-side identity: a cik-typed edge to the EDGAR company-ticker table. `edgar` is a ticker/exchange listing, not the CIK universe, so it covers a small part of the registrants this crosswalk keys on; the direction of containment runs neither way. Join by rendering `edgar.cik` (an integer) as text and comparing it to `key` (text) — the rendering is exact, because no published CIK carries a leading zero.
joins.evidence: For key_type='cik' rows, `key` is the EDGAR Central Index Key as reported to SEC EDGAR. Where both sides hold the same registrant the values agree exactly; the shortfall is coverage, not disagreement — `edgar` is built from the SEC's company-tickers file, so its reach follows that file rather than the registrant population.
joins.name: edgar

joins.cardinality: partial — most left rows match; the remainder carry an LEI that is not in the GLEIF object this descriptor names. `coverage` is written into the built descriptor, not into this file — see `verifiedBy` below.
joins.description: GLEIF-side identity: the LEI each edge resolved to. Join `lei` to `gleif.lei` directly — both sides are text and no rendering is involved.

evidence.comparison: normalized company name (exact, then Jaro-Winkler tiers)
evidence.method: Fellegi-Sunter probabilistic record linkage (Splink), frozen model, for the operating-company tail; official SEC/GLEIF registration for authoritative edges
evidence.precision: exact normalized-name matches auto-confirmed (~95% precision, spot-checked); name-only fuzzy matches surfaced as candidate, not confirmed
evidence.tie_break: ISSUED > LAPSED > RETIRED, then US jurisdiction

joins.name: gleif

x-joins.verifiedBy: datasets/edgar_gleif/scripts/crosswalk_join.py — the same script both writes and checks `coverage`. Run with `--write`, right after `describe`, it measures each join above against this build's own Parquet and writes `coverage` into datapackage.json (arcform.yaml step `derive_join_coverage`). Run with no flags, it re-measures against the published objects instead and fails if the committed `coverage` disagrees.
